From: Sam Green <sam.green@openlib.org>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:23:12 -0800
Subject: Interested in Redwood for OpenLib — GitHub integration questions

Hi Redwood team,

I signed up for the hosted trial yesterday after seeing your repo and a mention on GitHub Discussions for OpenLib (https://github.com/openlib/openlib-core). I'm an engineering lead for the OpenLib project — we build an open-source search/indexing layer for scholarly content. We're evaluating options for embeddings and semantic search, and several maintainers recommended Redwood for low-latency inference and your GitHub examples.

Quick questions before a demo:
- Do you have an official integration guide for GitHub-hosted projects (CI hooks, auth with PATs, repo -> embeddings pipeline)?
- How do you handle self-hosted embeddings/Private deployments vs hosted API for OSS projects? Any free/open credits for OSS projects?

Would love a quick demo to see how Redwood fits into our workflow and ask integration-specific questions. Our preferred timezone is PST.

Thanks,
Sam Green
Engineering Lead, OpenLib
sam.green@openlib.org
https://github.com/samgreen

A couple quick questions so we make the demo useful:
- Primary use case: code search/semantic search across repos, or embeddings for ranking/metadata?
- Ballpark monthly inference volume (requests or tokens) and latency target (p50/p95)?

Thanks Dev — appreciate the quick reply.

Primary use case is semantic search across our public repos and embeddings for ranking in our search UI. Volume is currently small during indexing runs (~50-100k embeddings/month) but we expect spikes during community-driven indexing events. Latency target is p95 < 200ms for user-facing search.

I can do Fri Mar 6 at 11:00 AM PST.

Also to clarify: we prefer hosted for initial eval but will need to understand Private/VPC options for governance for some contributors. Do you have an engineer who can speak to repo CI integration (e.g., auto-embed on merge)? Our repo: https://github.com/openlib/openlib-core

Sam
--
